opt_out_line: If this isn't for you, just let me know and I won't email again.
avoid_phrases: I hope this finds you well
following up on my last email

examples.situation: first email, they are hiring salespeople
examples.subject: two new account executives
examples.body: You are hiring two account executives for your new Singapore office. Reps who start without a target list spend their first weeks building one by hand. We research the companies, check which ones fit and choose when to write, so the new reps start with warm names. Who is building their first list for them?

examples.situation: first email, a launch they announced
examples.subject: the new billing module
examples.body: You launched a billing module for freight forwarders this month. A launch usually means a few busy weeks of finding the right accounts to tell. We research the companies, check which ones fit and choose when to write, so your reps start from a short list. How are they picking who to tell first?

examples.situation: first email, no hiring or news, written from who their customers are
examples.subject: selling to logistics firms
examples.body: Your customers are mostly mid-size logistics firms, a market where a good prospect list takes real digging. We research those companies, work out which ones fit and pick the moment to contact them, so your reps spend their time on conversations. Who builds those lists today?

examples.subject: Re: two new account executives
examples.body: One more thought on the new hires. The research they do in month one is the part we take over, which leaves them more time with buyers. If the timing is wrong, tell me and I will come back after your next quarter.

examples.situation: last follow-up, final and leaves the door open
examples.subject: Re: two new account executives
examples.body: This is my last note, so I will not clutter your inbox. If prospecting time becomes a bottleneck for the new reps, I will gladly show you how we handle the research. Either way, good luck with the hiring push.
